classification.difficultyReason: Match coefficients to the prescribed cosine-sum form, retaining its minus sign, then determine amplitude and the first-quadrant angle.

content.prompt: Express the following in the form $R\cos(x+\alpha)$.

answer.worked:
Expand the requested form and equate coefficients.
$$\begin{align*}\cos x-\sqrt{3}\sin x&=R\cos\alpha\cos x-R\sin\alpha\sin x\\R\cos\alpha&=1\\R\sin\alpha&=\sqrt{3}\\R&=\sqrt{1^2+(\sqrt{3})^2}=2\\\tan\alpha&=\sqrt{3}\end{align*}$$
Both $\cos\alpha$ and $\sin\alpha$ are positive, so choose $\alpha$ in the first quadrant.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=\frac{\pi}{3}\\\cos x-\sqrt{3}\sin x&=2\cos\left(x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\end{align*}$$

Expand the requested form and equate coefficients.
$$\begin{align*}12\cos x-5\sin x&=R\cos\alpha\cos x-R\sin\alpha\sin x\\R\cos\alpha&=12\\R\sin\alpha&=5\\R&=\sqrt{12^2+5^2}=13\\\tan\alpha&=\frac{5}{12}\end{align*}$$
Both $\cos\alpha$ and $\sin\alpha$ are positive, so choose $\alpha$ in the first quadrant.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{12}\right)\\12\cos x-5\sin x&=13\cos\left(x+\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{12}\right)\right)\end{align*}$$

Expand the requested form and equate coefficients.
$$\begin{align*}2\cos x-2\sin x&=R\cos\alpha\cos x-R\sin\alpha\sin x\\R\cos\alpha&=2\\R\sin\alpha&=2\\R&=\sqrt{2^2+2^2}=2\sqrt{2}\\\tan\alpha&=1\end{align*}$$
Both $\cos\alpha$ and $\sin\alpha$ are positive, so choose $\alpha$ in the first quadrant.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=\frac{\pi}{4}\\2\cos x-2\sin x&=2\sqrt{2}\cos\left(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\end{align*}$$
